title: Minimum Cost of Buying Candies With Discount
statement:
A store runs a deal on candies: each time you pay for two candies, you may also take one more candy at no charge, provided its price is at most the cheaper of the two you paid for. You may also pay for a candy without using the deal.

`cost[i]` is the price of candy `i`. You must end up with every candy. Return the smallest total amount you have to pay.
notes:
## Intuition

Every free candy needs two paid candies that cost at least as much. To save the most, the free candies should be as expensive as possible. The single most expensive candy can never be free (nothing paid costs more), nor can the second; but the third most expensive one can ride along with the top two. Repeating that idea on what remains shows the best plan: after sorting from most to least expensive, every third candy is free. Trying every grouping also works, but it explodes combinatorially.

## Approach

1. Sort `cost` in descending order.
2. Walk the sorted prices with index `i`.
3. Positions `2, 5, 8, ...` (where `i % 3 === 2`) are the free candies: each is no pricier than the two just before it, so skip them.
4. Add every other price to `total` and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`cost = [1, 2, 3]` sorts to `[3, 2, 1]`. At `i = 0` add 3 (`total = 3`), at `i = 1` add 2 (`total = 5`), and `i = 2` is the free slot, so 1 is skipped. The answer is `5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- Sorting ascending and skipping every third from the start frees the wrong candies; group from the expensive end.
- With fewer than three candies (or a leftover one or two at the end) nothing is free; the modulo check handles this naturally.
- The free candy only has to be no pricier than the cheaper paid one, so equal prices are fine.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cost` | candy prices, sorted from most to least expensive |
| `total` | amount paid so far |
| `i` | position in the sorted prices |

narration.2: Sort the prices from most to least expensive so each group of three is as costly as possible.
narration.4: Visit every candy in sorted order.
narration.5: The third candy of each group is no pricier than the two before it, so it is the free one.
narration.6: Skip paying for the free candy.
